geometry_edits.rationale: Turn the dominant box mutation into a tapered mass so the silhouette and section begin to respond to program rather than remaining generic.
Taper along the long axis to produce a clearer street-building profile.
Keep the base substantial at the ground edge.
Introduce a modest upper reduction to create hierarchy without over-fragmentation.
Insert an access-side notch to produce a legible ground response and public threshold.
Make the opening proportionally visible but still compact.
Widen the entry seam enough to read as public ground articulation.

rationale: The four-view diagram is internally consistent and the geometry compiles cleanly, but the massing is still a very generic rectilinear block with a shallow central cut. It is coherent across views and contained by the parcel, yet it does not meaningfully translate the neighborhood_living brief: the dominant gesture remains box-like, the courtyard is not read as an active public threshold toward the access edge, and the section/roof offers little program-specific spatial consequence. The visible void is real but weakly public; it functions more as a subtraction from a compact box than as a legible street-facing ground response. The overall result is repairable, but currently under-articulated for the required active-edge neighborhood condition.

warnings: Primary access edge is not convincingly animated; the access response reads closed/opposite rather than open.
The courtyard/void lacks clear alignment to the verified frontage/access edge.
Sectional expression is too flat/generic for the referenced neighborhood-public-space logic.
Do not treat the central opening as sufficient on its own; it needs stronger ground-level public consequence.
